questions.question: Which method can separate insoluble sand from water?
questions.feedback: Use filtration because the filter retains solid particles larger than its pores.

questions.question: Which method can recover salt from a salt solution without collecting the water?
questions.feedback: Use evaporation because the water leaves as vapour and the salt remains.

questions.question: Which method can collect water from salt water?
questions.feedback: Use distillation because water vapour is cooled and collected as a liquid.

questions.question: Which method can separate gravel from fine sand?
questions.feedback: Use sieving because the smaller grains pass through the mesh.

questions.question: Which method can remove iron filings from dry sand?
questions.feedback: Use magnetic separation because a magnet attracts the iron filings.

questions.question: Which method can separate soluble dyes in ink?
questions.feedback: Use paper chromatography because the dyes travel different distances on the paper.

questions.question: Which method can pour clear water away from settled mud?
questions.feedback: Use decanting because the settled solid can stay behind as the liquid is poured.

questions.question: Which method can separate layers of oil and water?
questions.feedback: Use separating funnel because the two liquids form layers and the lower one can drain first.
